subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To put a spoke in one’s wheel

options.text: To thwart someone in execution of one’s design
To leave someone without any provision

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom provided is **"To put a spoke in one’s wheel"** which refers to causing difficulties for someone or thwarting someone's plan.
